introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, 0550 Geography 1, June 2024, Ordinary Level. Multiple choice question paper, duration: one and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions. All questions carry equal marks. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Mark only one answer for each question; if you mark more than one answer you will score zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Do all your rough work in the question booklet.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 1-3 use the map in Fig. 1 (question 2 also uses its key); question 43 uses the settlement diagram in Fig. 2.

Hand-drawn settlement diagram: about forty small square houses crowded together where a road and a stream cross (Question 43).

questions.corrige_markdown: The scale printed under the map is $1 : 50\,000$. A representative fraction means that one unit on the map stands for 50 000 of the same unit on the ground, so 1 cm on the map represents 50 000 cm on the ground. Converting: $50\,000\ \text{cm} = 500\ \text{m} = 0.5\ \text{km}$. Option B uses the wrong number (25 000), and options C and D give kilometres, which would make 1 cm stand for thousands of kilometres, far larger than the Earth's circumference of roughly 40 000 km. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: 1 cm on the map represents 50,000 cm on the ground.
1 cm on the map represents 25,000 cm on the ground.
1 cm on the map represents 50,000 km on the ground.
1 cm on the map represents 25,000 km on the ground.

**2.** The actual direction of the church from the quarry is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Find the two symbols in the key. The church symbol (a small circle on a cross) is in the upper left part of the map, just right of the left margin and above the middle grid line. The quarry symbol (a row of small hachures) is in the lower right part of the map, near the 02 grid line. To go from the quarry to the church one must go up the page (north) and to the left (west), so the church lies to the **north west** of the quarry. On a map, north is at the top and west at the left unless a north arrow shows otherwise (none is printed here). **Answer: C.**

Use the map in Fig. 1 (Map of Okra, scale 1 : 50 000).

**3.** The physical shape of the landscape covered by the vegetation is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The vegetation symbols (small tree signs listed in the key) are scattered inside and around the set of closed, roughly circular contour lines in the middle of the map, labelled up to 130 m. Closed concentric contours that rise to a single summit show a rounded elevation. At about 130 m, with contours that are gently spaced, it is a **hill**, not a mountain (which would be much higher, with many closely packed contours). A cliff would be shown by contours that run together, and a plateau by a flat top with contours packed round its edge. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **4.** Which of the following can be a possible representation of administration functions on a map?
questions.corrige_markdown: Administrative functions are the work of government and public services: offices of the Divisional Officer or the council, town hall, courts, police and similar public buildings. Warehouses (storage and trade), factories (manufacturing) and spoil heaps (waste from mining or quarrying) belong to commercial, industrial and mining functions. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **5.** Which of the following pairs concerning functions of settlement is wrongly matched?
questions.corrige_markdown: Each pair links a function to a feature that shows it on a map. A campsite serves tourism, works (factories) show industrial function, and a chapel shows religious function. A park is an open space for recreation, not an administrative feature; administration is shown by public offices. So the pair "Administration and Park" is the wrong match. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **6.** When the earth comes between the sun and the moon it is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: When the Earth lies on the straight line between the Sun and the Moon (order Sun, Earth, Moon), the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon: this is a **lunar eclipse**, and it happens at full moon. In a solar eclipse it is the Moon that comes between the Sun and the Earth. "Earth's eclipse" and "light eclipse" are not terms used in geography. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **7.** What is the longitude of a place whose local Time is 4pm and GMT is 7pm?
questions.corrige_markdown: Local time is behind GMT (4 pm against 7 pm), so the place is **west** of the Greenwich meridian (the Sun reaches places in the east first). Time difference: $7 - 4 = 3\ \text{hours}$. The Earth turns $360^\circ$ in 24 hours, that is $15^\circ$ per hour, or 4 minutes per degree. Longitude: $3 \times 15^\circ = 45^\circ$. The place is at $45^\circ\text{W}$. Option B is the trap of forgetting that a place with slower time is in the west; C and D use the wrong number of degrees ($2 \times 15^\circ$). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **8.** The International Date Line is that line which when crossed from West to East,
questions.corrige_markdown: The International Date Line follows the $180^\circ$ meridian, with a few bends. East of it the calendar date is one day behind the date west of it. A traveller who crosses it from west to east therefore sets the calendar back by one day, so the same date is repeated: a **day is gained**. Crossing from east to west, the calendar is put forward by one day and a day is lost. Changes of one hour belong to the time zones (every $15^\circ$), not to the date line. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **9.** Identify the ODD statement below concerning the hydrological cycle.
questions.corrige_markdown: Statements A, C and D are correct: water circulates continuously, plants release vapour by transpiration, and evaporation from lakes, rivers and oceans lifts water into the air. Statement B is the odd one out because precipitation (rain, snow, hail) brings water **down** from the atmosphere to the earth's surface; it does not take water up. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Water moves continuously from the earth surface to the atmosphere and back to the earth surface.
Water is taken from the earth's surface to the atmosphere by precipitation.
Water vapour is emitted from plant leaves by a process called transpiration.
Water is taken from the earth's surface to the atmosphere by evaporation from the surface of lakes, rivers, stream and ocean.

questions.enonce_markdown: **10.** Evapo-transpiration is the loss of water
questions.corrige_markdown: Evapo-transpiration is the combined loss of water to the air by evaporation (from open water, soil and wet surfaces) and by transpiration (water vapour given off by plants). A definition must therefore include plants. Options A and D leave plants out, and option C leaves out evaporation. Option B is the only one that combines plants (transpiration) with water bodies (evaporation), so it is the best of the four. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: By water bodies and land surface.

questions.enonce_markdown: **11.** The main aspect that creates a distinction between weather and climate is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Weather and climate are described with the same elements (temperature, rainfall, pressure, wind, humidity) and are measured with the same instruments over the same place. What separates them is **time**: weather is the state of the atmosphere over a short period (hours or days), while climate is the average weather of a place over a long period, usually 30 years or more. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **12.** Lines showing equal values on weather maps: Isotherms, Isohels and Isobars correspond respectively to which group of elements?
questions.corrige_markdown: An isotherm joins places with equal temperature, an isohel joins places with equal amounts (duration) of sunshine, and an isobar joins places with equal atmospheric pressure. The group in the right order is temperature, sunshine and pressure. (Equal rainfall is shown by isohyets and equal wind speed by isotachs.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **13.** Temperatures are high (28°C), rainfall is high (2500mm), a long rainy season and a low temperature range are:
questions.corrige_markdown: The equatorial climate has a mean temperature of about 27 to 28 °C all year, a very small annual range (about 2 to 3 °C), rainfall above 2000 mm and a long rainy season with no real dry season. The tropical monsoon climate has a clearly marked dry season and a larger temperature range, the Mediterranean climate has hot dry summers and mild wet winters, and the tropical continental climate has a short rainy season, lower rainfall and a large range. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **14.** Winds that blow from sub-tropical high pressure belts to the temperate low pressure belts are called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Winds always blow from high to low pressure. The sub-tropical highs lie near $30^\circ$ N and S, the temperate (sub-polar) lows near $60^\circ$ N and S. Winds blowing poleward between them are deflected by the Earth's rotation and blow from the west: the **westerlies**. The trade winds blow from the sub-tropical highs towards the equatorial low, the polar easterlies from the polar highs, and monsoons reverse with the seasons. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **15.** When air is sinking and piling, what happens to the pressure of that area?
questions.corrige_markdown: Pressure is the weight of the air above a place. When air sinks and piles up over an area, more air presses on the surface, so atmospheric pressure is **high** (an anticyclone, with clear dry weather). Rising air does the opposite and gives low pressure. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **16.** The following are characteristics of a biome: trees have large trunks, broad leaves, buttress roots, little undergrowth. Identify the biome.
questions.corrige_markdown: Tall evergreen trees with large trunks, broad leaves and buttress roots (wide flat roots that support the tree in thin wet soil) are typical of the **tropical rainforest**. The dense canopy blocks sunlight, so little grows on the forest floor. Grassland has few trees, monsoon forest loses its leaves in the dry season and has a thicker undergrowth, and temperate deciduous forest has no buttress roots. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **17.** The soil type associated with the biome in question 16 is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The biome in question 16 is the tropical rainforest. Under its heavy rainfall and high temperature, minerals are leached out and iron and aluminium oxides remain, giving deep red **ferralitic** soils. Ferruginous soils belong to the drier savanna, alluvial soils form on river flood plains, and "lateritic" describes the hard iron crust (laterite) that can form when ferralitic soil is exposed and baked, not the soil type itself. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **18.** It includes all the living things in a given area, interacting with each other, and also with their non-living environments. This is referring to:
questions.corrige_markdown: An **ecosystem** is a community of living things (plants and animals) together with the non-living environment (soil, water, air, climate) with which they interact. Biomass is the mass of living matter, a food web is the set of feeding links, and energy flow is the movement of energy through those links. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **19.** A continental crust that contains minerals such as silica and alumina is called?
questions.corrige_markdown: The continental crust is rich in silica and alumina, so it is called **SIAL** (Si + Al). The oceanic crust, rich in silica and magnesium, is called SIMA. The mesosphere is part of the mantle and the Mohorovicic discontinuity is the boundary between the crust and the mantle. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **20.** Rocks formed by the cooling and solidification of molten material on the earth's surface are called?
questions.corrige_markdown: Molten rock that reaches the surface (lava) cools quickly and forms extrusive or **volcanic** rocks such as basalt. Plutonic rocks (granite) cool slowly deep inside the crust, sedimentary rocks form from deposited material, and metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **21.** Which evidence serves as proof to the theory that, present day continents broke up and moved horizontally?
questions.corrige_markdown: The theory of continental drift (Wegener) rests on the jigsaw fit of the coasts of South America and Africa, together with matching rocks and fossils across the ocean. Subduction zones are a result of plate movement, not proof of the break-up, and similar mountain heights or rainfall have no link with it. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **22.** Which of the following pairs are all examples of physical weathering processes?
questions.corrige_markdown: Physical (mechanical) weathering breaks rock without changing its chemistry: pressure release (unloading), temperature changes (expansion and contraction), freeze-thaw and frost action. Hydrolysis, oxidation, hydration and carbonation are chemical weathering processes. Only option A has two physical processes; in B, C and D at least one of the two is chemical. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **23.** The lifting and blowing of sand dust and gravel by wind is called?
questions.corrige_markdown: **Deflation** is the removal of loose sand, dust and small stones by the wind, which leaves hollows and stony surfaces (deflation hollows). Abrasion is the wearing away of rock by sand carried by the wind, attrition is the wearing down of the carried particles themselves, and plucking is glacial erosion. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **24.** Which of the following is a solution to the problem of global warming?
questions.corrige_markdown: Global warming is caused mainly by extra greenhouse gases, above all carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels and from deforestation. Planting new forests (afforestation) and replanting cut ones (reforestation) remove carbon dioxide from the air. The other three options would add greenhouse gases or pollutants. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**25.** 'There is water everywhere but none to drink'. Water scarcity here is best explained as:

*Options as printed:* A) Water available is contaminated.   B) Water available is for industrial use.   C) Water available is good for dipping animals.   D) Water available is not pipe borne.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The saying describes a place where there is plenty of water but it cannot be drunk. The most direct reading is that the water is polluted or contaminated (salt water, sewage, industrial waste), so it is unfit for drinking: this is scarcity of safe water. Option D (not pipe borne) is also possible if the saying is read as a lack of treated, piped supply, which is called economic water scarcity, and the question does not make clear which reading the examiners intended.

**Intended answer: A (Water available is contaminated).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **26.** Landslide commonly occurs in areas with:
questions.corrige_markdown: A landslide is the sudden movement of soil and rock down a slope under gravity, triggered above all by heavy rain on **steep slopes**, especially where the vegetation has been cleared. Highlands, plateaux and ridges are landforms; the slope angle is what makes the movement likely. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **27.** You happen to be in the classroom when an earthquake is taking place. What will be your immediate reaction to save yourself from death?
questions.corrige_markdown: Indoors, the standard advice is "drop, cover and hold on": get under a strong desk or table, which protects the head and body from falling objects and ceiling pieces, and stay there until the shaking stops. Running outside or to a tree during the shaking is dangerous because people are hurt by falling debris on the way, and lying on the ground leaves the body unprotected. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Run for shelter under a tree.

questions.enonce_markdown: **28.** Identify limestone features from the list below; i.Uvala ii. Polje iii. Talus iv.Doline v. Levee
questions.corrige_markdown: Limestone (karst) landscapes have solution features: a doline (a round surface hollow), an uvala (several dolines joined together) and a polje (a large flat-floored basin). A talus is a slope of loose rock fragments (scree) at the foot of a cliff, and a levee is a raised bank built by a river at flood time; neither is specific to limestone. The correct set is i, ii and iv. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**29.** The NICs (Newly Industrialized Countries) are found in which of the following stages of Rostow's model?

*Options as printed:* A) The take off stage.   B) Pre-condition for take off.   C) Drive to maturity.   D) Mass consumption stages.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rostow's model has five stages: traditional society, pre-conditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity and high mass consumption. Newly industrialised countries (for example South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore) have already passed the early industrial phase and have a wide range of manufactured goods and technology, which best matches the **drive to maturity**. Some textbooks place them in the take-off stage, so the examiners' key cannot be confirmed.

**Intended answer: C (Drive to maturity).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **30.** In an agricultural system, grains, eggs, vegetable and meat are examples of:
questions.corrige_markdown: A farm is a system. Inputs are what goes in (seeds, labour, fertilizer, capital), processes are the operations on the farm (ploughing, planting, harvesting), and outputs are what comes out. Grains, eggs, vegetables and meat are products of the farm, so they are **outputs**. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**31.** Which in the list below is a measure to improve on Tropical agriculture?

*Options as printed:* A) Crop rotation.   B) Land tenure.   C) Land diversification.   D) Hybridization.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Crop rotation, reforms of land tenure and the use of hybrid (improved, high-yielding) seeds can all help tropical farming, so the question does not isolate a single measure. If one option must be chosen as a technical measure to raise yields, hybridisation (planting improved varieties that give more and resist disease) is the most direct. Land tenure is a legal and social matter, and "land diversification" is not a standard term.

**Intended answer: D (Hybridization).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **32.** Timber resources such as iroko, sapelle, Ayos and mahogany are extracted from?
questions.corrige_markdown: Iroko, sapele, ayous (obeche) and mahogany are tall hardwood trees of the **tropical rainforest**, which in Cameroon is found mainly in the South, Centre, East and Littoral regions. Coniferous forests give softwood (pine, spruce) and temperate deciduous forests give oak or beech. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **33.** The following are solutions to the problems facing the fishing industry except:
questions.corrige_markdown: Overfishing and pollution are the main problems of the fishing industry. Fish ponds (aquaculture) reduce pressure on wild stocks, treating waste before disposal reduces water pollution, and a fishing holiday (closed season) lets stocks breed. Using nets of smaller size, that is a smaller mesh, catches young fish before they can breed and so makes overfishing worse; the real solution is to **increase** the mesh size. So "reducing the size of the net" is the exception. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Reducing the size of the net.

questions.enonce_markdown: **34.** Gold in the east region of Cameroon is mined through:
questions.corrige_markdown: Gold in the East Region is mostly worked by small-scale or artisanal miners, who pan and dig the gold-bearing gravels and sands of river beds and valleys, for example in the Batouri and Betare-Oya areas. This is **alluvial mining**. Submarine mining is done on the sea floor, drift mining follows a seam into a hillside, and underground mining needs shafts and heavy investment. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **35.** The advantage of using HEP over natural gas as source of energy is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Hydroelectric power uses flowing water, which is replaced by the water cycle, so it is **renewable**; natural gas is a fossil fuel that is used up and cannot be replaced in a human lifetime. HEP stations are expensive to build, dams are normally far from towns, and water is not "artificial". **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: HEP is artificial while natural gas is natural.
HEP stations are cheap to construct while natural gas stations are expensive to construct.
HEP is a renewable while natural gas is a non-renewable.
HEP stations are located in towns while natural gas stations are located in remote areas.

questions.enonce_markdown: **36.** The tendency for an industry to remain at its original location even though the factors which attracted it there are no longer relevant is called?
questions.corrige_markdown: **Industrial inertia** (or industrial momentum) is the tendency of an industry to stay where it began after the original advantages (raw material, power, cheap labour) have gone, because of the existing buildings, skilled workers, services and investment. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **37.** What makes Newly Industrialized Countries (NICs) different from other developing countries is that:
questions.corrige_markdown: NICs are developing countries whose economies have changed from dependence on primary activities (farming, mining) to the manufacture of goods, many of them exported. Their living standards are generally higher than other developing countries, they are not marked by instability, and their exports have grown, not fallen. Option C is the only true difference. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Their standard of living is lower.
They have all moved from primary activities to goods producing industrial activities.
They have reduced exports to other countries.

questions.enonce_markdown: **38.** Which mode of transport is most suitable for the transportation of bulky goods over long distances?
questions.corrige_markdown: Ships and barges can carry very large loads (oil, ores, timber, grain, containers) at the lowest cost per tonne and per kilometre, so **water transport** is the best for bulky goods over long distances. Air transport is fast but costly and limited in load, road transport is costly over long distances, and pipelines carry only liquids and gases. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **39.** Taxes levied on goods entering a country are called?
questions.corrige_markdown: A **tariff** is a tax (customs duty) charged on imported goods. A quota limits the quantity that may be imported, a subsidy is money paid by a government to help producers, and an embargo is a ban on trade with a country. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **40.** Eco-tourism involves: 1-Large scale influx of tourists into a country. 2-Travelling for business and leisure. 3-Visit to see natural flora and fauna. 4-Meant to protect, preserve and conserve nature. Select the pair that is correct
questions.corrige_markdown: Eco-tourism is responsible travel to natural areas to see flora and fauna (statement 3) in a way that protects and conserves nature (statement 4). Large-scale mass tourism (statement 1) and travel for business and leisure in general (statement 2) are not what defines eco-tourism. The correct pair is 3 and 4. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **41.** 'In a region named X, the population has more than doubled within the past two decades from 5 to 10 million inhabitants. While the available food resources have grown steadily. This phenomenal 'change' in population referred to above is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: A very fast rise in numbers, here a doubling in two decades while food supply grows only slowly, is called a **population explosion**. Growth from 5 million to 10 million in 20 years means that the population grew by 100 percent. "Optimum" would describe the best number for the resources, and growth or increase do not stress the speed. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **42.** As suggested by Thomas Malthus, what positive check can be used to control this alarming change in population numbers?
questions.corrige_markdown: Malthus argued that population grows faster than food and is held in check in two ways. Preventive checks reduce births (moral restraint, that is chastity and delayed marriage). Positive checks raise the death rate: famine, **disease** and war. Family planning (artificial birth control) was not one of his checks. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**43.** Identify the pattern of settlement shown in the diagram below:

![fig-2](gce-ol-geography-2024-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In the diagram the houses are crowded close together around the crossing of the road and the stream, which is the pattern of a **nucleated** (clustered) settlement. In a linear settlement the houses would be strung along a single road or river, in a dispersed settlement they would stand far apart, and "non nucleated" is another name for a scattered or dispersed pattern. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **44.** The creation of greenbelts and urban renewal are the most suitable solutions to problems of:
questions.corrige_markdown: A greenbelt is a ring of protected open land round a town that stops it from spreading outwards into the countryside: it controls **urban sprawl**. Urban renewal is the clearing and rebuilding of run-down areas of a town: it cures **urban decay**. Those two are the problems named in option A. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: House congestion and poor waste disposal.
Urban decay and poor waste disposal.

questions.enonce_markdown: **45.** An environmentally friendly method through which household waste can be managed is
questions.corrige_markdown: **Reuse** (together with reducing and recycling) cuts the amount of waste and causes no pollution. Burning waste pollutes the air, burying it can pollute soil and groundwater, and daily disposal only moves the waste to another place. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **46.** Multipurpose River development schemes may be carried out for all BUT ONE of the following reason: Identify the exception
questions.corrige_markdown: A multipurpose scheme has several aims: generating hydroelectric power, controlling floods, supplying water for irrigation (also for towns, fishing and navigation). Building a dam is not an aim: it is the means used to achieve these aims. So option D is the exception. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **47.** Which of the following mountains is found in the southern low plateau?
questions.corrige_markdown: The southern plateau of Cameroon is a low plateau of about 650 m, with a few inselbergs such as the Mbam Minkom hills near Yaounde. Mount Oku belongs to the western highlands (North West Region), the Mandara Mountains to the far north, and the Mambila mountains to the western border highlands with Nigeria. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **48.** Which of the following rivers flow into the Chad Basin?
questions.corrige_markdown: The **Logone**, rising in the Adamawa area and flowing north, joins the Chari and feeds Lake Chad in the inland Chad Basin. The Wouri, Sanaga and Mungo flow south-west to the Atlantic Ocean (Gulf of Guinea). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **49.** The mad rush by Cameroonian intellectual youths to foreign countries in search of 'greener pastures' is attributed to:
questions.corrige_markdown: "Greener pastures" means better opportunities. Educated young people who cannot find jobs at home leave to look for work and better pay abroad (the brain drain), so the main cause is **unemployment**. Tourism, conferences and medical care are short stays for other reasons. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**50.** Which of the following is a WRONG match?

| | HEP Project | River |
|---|---|---|
| A | Memve'le | Ntem |
| B | Mekin | Dja |
| C | Lom pangar | Sanaga |
| D | Lagdo | Benue |

*Options as printed:* A) Memve'le - Ntem.   B) Mekin - Dja.   C) Lom pangar - Sanaga.   D) Lagdo - Benue.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Memve'ele dam is on the Ntem River, the Mekin dam on the Dja River and the Lagdo dam on the Benue River, so A, B and D are right. The Lom Pangar dam is built on the Lom River, near its meeting with the Pangar, in the upper Sanaga basin; the Sanaga itself is formed further downstream, so pairing the project with "Sanaga" is the least exact match and is the one marked wrong here. The examiners' key cannot be confirmed.

**Intended answer: C (Lom pangar - Sanaga).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
